package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner;

      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner. Stored and returned in E.164 form.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[+0-9 ()-]*$'
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the pet owner was registered. Defaults to the current server date when not supplied.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-

          type: boolean

## Summary

Implemented `namesakeCount` on owner creation — the number of existing owners sharing the same first and last name (case-insensitively), computed before the new owner is saved, persisted, and returned on `GET /api/owners/{id}`.

Changes, each kept to a single responsibility:

1. **`Namesakes.java`** (new helper, package-private) — canonical name matching: two owners are namesakes when first and last name match after trim/whitespace-collapse/lower-case. Mirrors the existing `Households` / `CustomerCode` helper style so the comparison logic lives in one place.

2. **`CountNamesakes.java`** (new function) — reads the built `@Val Owner` and the `OwnerRepository`, counts existing owners matching via `Namesakes.matches`, and stores it with `owner.setNamesakeCount(...)`. Because it runs before `save`, the count excludes the new owner.

3. **`owners.POST.yml`** — wired `countNamesakes` into the pipeline between `assignCustomerCode` and `save`, under the same `transaction` governance as its neighbours.

4. **`Owner.java`** — added the persisted `namesakeCount` (`namesake_count` column) field with getter/setter and a `toString` entry.

5. **`OwnerMapper.java`** — added `@Mapping(target = "namesakeCount", ignore = true)` to `toOwner(OwnerFieldsDto)` (consistent with the existing `customerCode`/`householdId` ignores); the `Owner → OwnerDto` mapping picks the field up by name automatically.

6. **`openapi.yml`** — added a read-only `namesakeCount` integer to the `Owner` response schema.

7. **schema.sql** (hsqldb/h2/mysql/postgres) — added the `namesake_count` column; the test profile uses `hsqldb` with `ddl-auto=none`, so the column must exist in the schema script.

The new `AcceptanceTest.coreCountsNamesakes` passes, and the full test suite is green (`BUILD SUCCESS`, 0 failures/errors).
